Thanks for the clear ask, Sanjay — happy to outline our standard execution pattern and options. Short answer: we can accept AdobeSign or DocuSign, but we have a preferred envelope configuration to ensure auditability and smooth ingestion into our compliance store. Details below.

Preferred (recommended, fastest): DocuSign envelope we send with signing order:
1) Acme Legal (Rina) — Sign and initial
2) Acme Procurement (procurement@acme.com) — Sign and initial
3) Redwood Authorized Signatory (VP, Legal or CFO) — Countersign (final)

If you send AdobeSign, we require the completed PDF plus the AdobeSign audit log (PDF log or CSV) and a copy of the Evidence Report. DocuSign provides a Certificate of Completion automatically; for AdobeSign we ask you to attach the equivalent audit package.

Redwood requirements / verification checks:
- Signer email must match the Acme corporate address on file (procurement@acme.com / rina.kapoor@acme.com).
- If someone outside those emails will sign, we need a short LOA (email from the signee's manager + procurement) and a scanned ID for high-risk contracts (we'll escalate).
- Completed PDF + audit log must be delivered to redwood-dpa-executions@redwood.ai and copied to me.

For our internal signatory: VP Legal (Vanessa Ortiz) will countersign by default. If I'm unavailable, Marissa Cole (Head of Legal Ops) or Alex Martinez (CFO) may countersign as fallback — we'll document that in the envelope as alternate signers with conditional routing.

Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood) will create a DocuSign envelope as a canary (test envelope with a short cover sheet) and route to Rina first.
- If Acme confirms AdobeSign only, please send a test completed PDF + evidence report to our dpa inbox so our Legal Ops team can validate format and acceptance.

I'll loop Karthik to confirm the exact DocuSign settings (ID verification level, require phone/email OTP, and whether we need signer type = "individual" enforced).

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

Couple of quick items from Legal (checklist we enforce for execution pickup):

1) Envelope configuration:
   - Require signer email AND authentication by DocuSign Email OTP.
   - Set signer order (sequential) as Vanessa described; allow alternate signers but require LOA in the envelope comments.

2) Evidence we must retain:
   - Final executed PDF (flattened).
   - Certificate of Completion / Audit Report (DocuSign or AdobeSign).
   - Envelope metadata (envelope ID, envelope creation/sent/completed timestamps).

3) Delegation / LOA:
   - If Acme wants a delegated signer, we need an LOA from the delegated signer's manager/owner + procurement confirmation. LOA can be an attachment to the envelope or a separate signed PDF sent to redwood-dpa-executions@redwood.ai.

4) Countersign timing:

5) Audit retention:
   - Once completed, Legal Ops will pull the envelope artifacts and store them in the DPA executions bucket (s3://redwood-dpa-executions) with a metadata record in the contract binder (HubSpot deal 8452).

Attaching our internal execution checklist (DPA_execution_checklist.pdf) for your reference.

If Acme insists on AdobeSign only, ask them to send a completed package to redwood-dpa-executions@redwood.ai for verification before countersign.
